ownership_reason: Only the gold decides where the walk over the starts stops: hop 4 lays the weights out from zero and records one start per entry, hops 1 to 3 pass the index or the point along (hop 2 draws the single deviate). The gold's contract is the index of the interval that holds the point; the last interval holds every point at or above its start, because there is no next interval to move on to. The variant walks past the last interval and reads a start that does not exist, raising inside the gold, so no caller can take its result and recover it. The convention is pinned outside the gold: StepFunction.value gives a point at or past the last abscissa the last ordinate (StepFunctionTest::testSomeValues: f.value(30) and f.value(+inf) give the last step; testEndpointBehavior), PolynomialSplineFunction.value gives the last knot to the last piece; DiscreteRealDistributionTest::testSample and DiscreteIntegerDistributionTest::testSample pass through the chain (every draw inside the starts).
